questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the place was somewhat different from my home culture (Denmark) but at the same time safe and organized. In addition, it was crucial that the surrounding area had a lot of attractions, either driving distance or flight for weekend getaways.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Very easy. Either by my own school or by the host.
Either in person at school, website or email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I did not get any special assistance.
But I got all the mandatory, nice to haves: an overview of facilities, courses, clubs etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
They have huge facebook groups w many private opportunities. 
Otherwise, the official leasing websites are easy.
And it was safe and fast.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is cheaper and you can get good deals using Facebook and subleasers instead of taking over official lease.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You go online and look at course catalogues for previous years.
You get approval from professor if needed (fast and easy).
You go online and check the boxed and they let you know if you can take the courses.
You can easily cancel or enroll in new courses (I did twice)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Website, school officials, professors, a help desk at school, my own university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If in doubt whether you want to take a course ask a professor.
Take it easy. You can attend first couple of lectures and THEN select what you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Low academic level compared to similar courses in Denmark in my field.
Professors are fine and facilities are good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took 3 400-courses which are similar to 4th year MA courses in Denmark
But these were way easier than the same in Denmark

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar: just lectures, assignments, exams etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECN 436 International Trade Theory
ECN 453 Industrial Organization
CIS 412 Business Machine Learning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Only this one:
ECN 436 International Trade Theory

The professor is very knowledgable and the topics are super relevant and draw lines to real world applications.

The other ones are not 400-course level

Food is more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
A lot of culturel ones and sports.
I joined the jewish ones.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Engage in Greek Life for the fun of it.
And join sports club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The canyons up state
Vegas
Texas
California
Utah
Central America

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay. Language is easy and people are all western.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Bond over how American we are in europe.
Just engage in clubs w locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Not as humble as Scandinavia
People seem superficial and hard to really bond i feel

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How big everything is and so many options for everything.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Dont focus too much on studies and enjoy the state and all around it
2. Americans are different, especially in a red GOP state as AZ. But its fun
3. Engage in as many clubs to get a sense of it all

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Especially in the beginning of the stay, engage in activities to meet people.
You will be alone for some time, but that is also an important experience

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Putting myself out there and restarting my life.
New hobbies, new people, new food etc.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To fit in the American culture fully.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
